topic: Dedalus ORBIS: what it can and cannot do today for data access, search and AI
summary: ORBIS is the market-leading hospital information system in German-speaking countries and is used in more than 40 UKM clinics. Official UKM pages and peer-reviewed studies show that research queries reach structured and free-text entries but not PDFs, and that much ORBIS content was free text (for example half of the prescriptions in a Dresden study). Dedalus says the same in its own publications: information is hidden in free text and requires navigation through modules and forms. Dedalus lists AI drafting, speech, coding and risk functions as available in 2026, while the assistant that answers questions over the record (ORBIS Buddy) was announced in its agentic form in October 2026 and has no independent evaluation. No ORBIS-specific usability score was found, and KLAS ranks it best among DACH vendors, so criticism should address the document-centred design of the whole market.

findings.claim: UKM uses ORBIS in more than 40 clinics, on an 8,700 GB Oracle database with 7,938 users (status July 2020).
findings.detail: Reported by a Muenster team (psychiatry and medical informatics) in a feasibility study. The same paper counts over 1,300 ORBIS installations in DACH and calls it market leader. Figures are six years old.
findings.number: 8,700 GB; 7,938 users; 1,927 sessions per day; >40 clinics
findings.quote: The EHR system has an 8700 GB Oracle database, 7938 users, and 1927 user sessions per day
findings.source: Blitz et al., Design and Implementation of an Informatics Infrastructure for Standardized Data Acquisition, JMIR Ment Health 8(6):e26681
findings.talk_use: Opening number for the local setting; state 'as of 2020'.

findings.claim: The Muenster team had to extend ORBIS themselves to obtain standardized, exportable research data.
findings.detail: They found that ORBIS did not support standardized form metadata, clinical data or annotated data sets, and built the SMA:T extension (CDISC ODM) with 19 forms and 241 items. State of the product as of 2021; ORBIS U now advertises SNOMED CT and LOINC. It does not mean that no data can be exported.
findings.quote: does not currently support standardized form metadata, clinical data, or annotated data sets
findings.source: Blitz et al., JMIR Ment Health 8(6):e26681
findings.talk_use: Local peer-reviewed evidence that forms do not automatically give reusable data.

findings.claim: UKM's ORBIS study module can query structured and free-text data documented in ORBIS, but cannot search inside PDF documents.
findings.detail: MeDIC page on the module that came out of the BMBF project KISRek. Nightly queries fill a work list of candidate patients; more than 80 studies supported. The page has no date, so verify with MeDIC before showing it.
findings.quote: An automatic search for information in PDF-documents is not possible.
findings.source: MeDIC Muenster, Study module
findings.talk_use: Best single local quote: the research search stops at PDFs, which is where document extraction starts.

findings.claim: Researchers at UKM can request ORBIS data extracts, delivered anonymized or pseudonymized as a printout or an Excel sheet.
findings.detail: Offered by MeDIC with UKM IT through an intranet form; criteria such as diagnoses, demographics and lab values. Undated page.
findings.quote: provided anonymized or pseudonymized as a print or excel worksheet
findings.source: MeDIC Muenster, ORBIS Data extraction
findings.talk_use: Practical takeaway for doctoral candidates, and a picture of the current interface between care and research.

findings.claim: An ORBIS module built in Muenster registers study participants, pseudonymizes and randomizes them inside ORBIS.
findings.detail: MeDIC states that more than 10 clinics, over a quarter of UKM clinics, use it. It shows that ORBIS can be extended locally and that research use inside ORBIS works when data are structured. Undated.
findings.quote: The structured recording of studies and their participants enables study evaluations to be automated.
findings.source: MeDIC Muenster, Study patient management in ORBIS
findings.talk_use: Fair counterweight: ORBIS does support research when someone builds the structure.

findings.claim: Dedalus itself says that getting at information in a hospital information system still requires navigating modules, views and forms.
findings.detail: From the press release of 22 October 2026 on ORBIS Buddy with Corti. The statement is about hospital information systems in general and motivates the product.
findings.quote: erfordern jedoch weiterhin die Navigation durch verschiedene Module, Ansichten und Formulare
findings.source: Dedalus and Corti press release
findings.talk_use: Vendor's own words for the problem slide; very recent and hard to dispute.

findings.claim: Dedalus's Chief Medical Officer said that hospital systems often only imitate the paper chart instead of connecting data.
findings.detail: Customer magazine interview (DIREKT 2/2024) on the app ORBIS U Diagnosen und Probleme. A product manager adds that the information was usually in ORBIS, but often hidden in isolated free-text fields or coarse billing diagnoses.
findings.quote: Außerdem imitieren die Systeme häufig nur die Papierakte, anstatt Daten zu vernetzen
findings.source: Dedalus DIREKT 2/2024, Paradigmenwechsel in der Patientensicht
findings.talk_use: Quote slide: document-centred design, admitted by the vendor.

findings.claim: Dedalus states that a large part of the data in most hospital systems, including ORBIS, is unstructured.
findings.detail: Guest article in DIREKT 1/2024, naming findings, letters and notes. No percentage is given. The same article says Dedalus develops NLP that maps text to SNOMED, ICD-10, ATC and LOINC, and mentions about 300,000 outpatient bills per year at UKM as a use case.
findings.quote: ein großer Teil der Daten unstrukturiert – zum Beispiel in Befunden, Briefen, Notizen – vor, so auch in ORBIS
findings.source: Dedalus DIREKT 1/2024, Digitale Revolution: die nächsten Schritte
findings.talk_use: Can replace unsourced percentages of unstructured data with an ORBIS-specific vendor statement.

findings.claim: In a Dresden study of ORBIS medication data, only 47.7% of 1.77 million inpatient prescriptions were structured.
findings.detail: University Hospital Dresden, ORBIS curve module KURV, 2016 to 2020; ICU and chemotherapy were excluded because those systems were fully structured. String matching raised the share to 85.2%. Older module; ORBIS Medication may differ.
findings.source: Reinecke et al., Assessment and Improvement of Drug Data Structuredness From Electronic Health Records, JMIR Med Inform 11:e40312
findings.talk_use: Answers 'last dose change?': half of the prescriptions were text, and processing the text recovered most of them.

findings.claim: In an exploratory Cologne test, clinicians needed 172 s with a purpose-built dashboard instead of 635 s in ORBIS to collect the facts for a treatment decision.
findings.detail: MEDA-PKD, 7 clinicians experienced in ADPKD, facts needed for tolvaptan; ORBIS had been filled in a structured way beforehand. Not blinded, small n, study by the developers. The SUS of 90.4 refers to the dashboard; no SUS for ORBIS is reported. The supplement was not read.
findings.quote: MEDA-PKD resulted in highly significant time savings (mean 72.4%, group means 634.5 to 172.3 s
findings.source: Grundmann et al., MEDA-PKD, npj Digital Medicine 2026, doi 10.1038/s41746-026-03267-0
findings.talk_use: The only direct ORBIS timing found: same question, question-centred view more than three times faster. Show n=7.

findings.claim: For a UKM-led LLM study on liver cancer (106 patients), reports were retrieved from ORBIS as PDF files and merged into one anonymized PDF per patient.
findings.detail: Sci Rep 2026, UKM radiology first author. Experts needed on average 9.3 min per patient only for data availability checks and liver function analysis; GPT answered in under 2 min. The paper calls for human oversight. Patients with missing data were excluded, which favours the model.
findings.quote: retrieved as PDF files from the Clinical Information System (CIS; Orbis, Dedalus, Milan, Italy)
findings.source: Masthoff et al., Performance of GPT-based large language models in hepatocellular carcinoma stratification, Sci Rep 16:18342
findings.talk_use: Local example of both the problem (PDF export) and the method (LLM on documents).

findings.claim: Dedalus announced ORBIS Buddy as an agent layer over ORBIS that answers questions about the patient and prepares actions in natural language.
findings.detail: Press release of 22 Oct 2026, introduction to start in DACH, described as an early application phase. A June 2026 brochure lists Buddy 2.0 under 'Ausblick'. Dedalus claims each action is validated, auditable and traceable; no independent evaluation was found, and linking to source passages is not described in what was read.
findings.quote: ist jede Aktion validiert, auditierbar und nachvollziehbar
findings.source: Dedalus and Corti press release
findings.talk_use: Q&A: 'Will ORBIS do this itself?' Announced a month ago, not evaluated; ask whether each answer links to its source passage.

findings.claim: Dedalus lists five AI functions as available in ORBIS in June 2026: speech assistant, AI epicrisis draft, text engine, clinalytix risk alerts and RICO coding.
findings.detail: Vendor brochure; its claim that the speech assistant takes over 80 to 90% of documentation work has no source. The epicrisis draft is built from structured ORBIS data and must be validated by the physician. Listed as outlook: Buddy 2.0, Speech Assistant 2.0, next-generation dictation, outpatient coding.
findings.quote: generiert auf Basis strukturierter Behandlungsdaten aus ORBIS automatisch einen ersten Textentwurf
findings.source: Dedalus, Künstliche Intelligenz in ORBIS (brochure)
findings.talk_use: Table 'what ORBIS ships vs announces'. Shipped functions write text, code or alert; overviews over the record are in the outlook.

findings.claim: Dedalus plans to let physicians check extracted medical facts one by one before the final text is generated.
findings.detail: Announced for Speech Assistant 2.0. It applies to spoken encounters; the brochure does not mention links into older documents.
findings.quote: präsentiert das System die extrahierten medizinischen Fakten einzeln
findings.source: Dedalus, Künstliche Intelligenz in ORBIS (brochure)
findings.talk_use: Supports the chain-of-proof argument: the market leader also moves to review at fact level.

findings.claim: Vivantes, a large ORBIS customer, reported that most of the tools it pilots and tests show no added value.
findings.detail: Dedalus customer magazine article on clinalytix Sepsis and Delir, in a passage about AI and alternatives. Vivantes introduced clinalytix in 2024 after a silent run; departments very familiar with a disease saw no notable benefit. Qualitative report, printed by the vendor.
findings.quote: Wir pilotieren und testen viel – und stellen in den meisten Fällen tatsächlich keinen Mehrwert fest.
findings.source: Dedalus DIREKT 2/2024, So wird KI fit für die klinische Routine
findings.talk_use: Sober counter-voice from practice.

findings.claim: A hospital introducing ORBIS U reports that users suffer from switching between the old and the new ORBIS world, with more than 200 applications and modules attached to ORBIS.
findings.detail: Managing director of Klinikum Dritter Orden, Munich, in the Dedalus magazine 1/2025. The hospital is a Dedalus reference site and otherwise positive.
findings.quote: Die Anwender leiden zunehmend unter dem Wechsel zwischen alter und neuer Welt
findings.source: Dedalus DIREKT 1/2025, Gemeinsam digital stark
findings.talk_use: Why waiting for ORBIS U is not a short-term answer.

findings.claim: ORBIS U is a new microservice, browser-based platform with SNOMED CT and LOINC, introduced step by step next to classic ORBIS.
findings.detail: Dedalus page. The 2025 annual report names Medication, Patient Chart, wound management, Clinical Problems and Assisted Coding as developed modules. A Dedalus product director said in 2025 that not everything is finished.
findings.quote: Im Unterschied zum holistischen ORBIS besteht das System aus technisch separaten Bausteinen
findings.source: Dedalus, ORBIS U product page
findings.talk_use: Background for Q&A on ORBIS vs ORBIS U.

findings.claim: Dedalus product managers said in 2024 that the mandated FHIR interface ISiK could not yet match HL7 v2 and that first real projects would arrive in 2026 at the earliest.
findings.detail: DIREKT 1/2024. ORBIS received ISiK stage 1 confirmation on 16 May 2023; Dedalus says later stages are not rolled out automatically to customers. Vendor view; gematik register not checked.
findings.quote: frühestens 2026 die ersten Projekte in der Versorgungslandschaft ankommen werden
findings.source: Dedalus DIREKT 1/2024, Alles Standard, oder?
findings.talk_use: Why 'just use FHIR' is not a full answer yet.

findings.claim: The Dedalus archive HYDMedia G6 offers a FHIR server through which external clients can search and read documents by patient or encounter.
findings.detail: Vendor flyer, November 2025, claiming ISiK conformity including document exchange stage 3. It delivers documents with metadata (DocumentReference, Binary), so content still has to be read from text. Whether UKM runs HYDMedia is not known.
findings.quote: Der HYDMedia G6 FHIR-Server ist vollständig konform mit dem gematik-Standard
findings.source: Dedalus, FHIR-Integration in HYDMedia G6
findings.talk_use: A technical door for document pipelines exists; it opens to documents, so extraction remains necessary.

findings.claim: A German hospital justified buying without competition because Dedalus integrated only one medication system deeply and offered no specified interfaces for others.
findings.detail: TED award notice, Klinikum Dahme-Spreewald, 7.93 million EUR, 2023. This is the buyer's legal justification for a direct award, so it has an interest in stressing the lack of alternatives.
findings.quote: bietet keine spezifizierten Schnittstellen an, um eine vergleichbare Integration mit einem Drittsystem zu etablieren
findings.source: TED notice 458974-2023
findings.talk_use: Official document for the vendor lock-in point.

findings.claim: KLAS found that interviewed customers of German-language EHR vendors call for improvement, citing development delays, weak support, outdated technology and usability.
findings.detail: KLAS blog on DACH KIS 2025; no runaway leaders. The statement covers all vendors. Dedalus is Best in KLAS for DACH 2024, 2025 and 2026. The full report is behind a paywall.
findings.quote: interviewed customers cite delays in development, weak support, outdated technology, and usability challenges
findings.source: KLAS Research, DACH KIS 2025: A Market at a Crossroads
findings.talk_use: Fairness: ORBIS is rated best in a market in which users expect more.

findings.claim: Dedalus claims 43% of acute care contracts in DACH, citing KLAS 2025.
findings.detail: Vendor press release; another Dedalus release speaks of over 800 ORBIS hospitals. In Dedalus's reading of KLAS 2025, 75% of tenders were won since 2020 and 100% of interviewed sites would choose ORBIS again; individual users ask for a better roadmap, usability and mobile apps. No independent German share figure was found.
findings.quote: 43 % Marktanteil bei Akutversorgungsverträgen in der DACH-Region
findings.source: Dedalus, ORBIS im KLAS Report
findings.talk_use: Say 'market leader in DACH according to vendor and KLAS'.

findings.claim: Charite chose Epic in December 2025 for about 200 million EUR after excluding Dedalus on formal grounds.
findings.detail: heise, 12 Dec 2025; full rollout planned by end of 2029. Dedalus withdrew without further legal action (9 Oct 2025) and criticised the tender. Goettingen and Cologne, in contrast, announced ORBIS.
findings.number: about 200 million EUR; complete by end of 2029
findings.source: heise online, Epic Systems: US provider wins Charité tender
findings.talk_use: Q&A: would another system help? Migration takes years, and old documents remain.

findings.claim: SAP ends regular maintenance of IS-H in 2027 and paid extended maintenance in 2030, which leads many hospitals to replace their systems.
findings.detail: Law firm overview, May 2026. Roland Berger (Dec 2025, 600 managers) finds 30% planning a change of hospital system; 46% expect the main tender wave in 2027. Whether UKM uses IS-H was not documented in the sources read.
findings.source: Taylor Wessing, IS-H-Ablösung
findings.talk_use: Context: many hospitals will be busy migrating until about 2030.

findings.claim: German hospitals score 42.4 of 100 in the second DigitalRadar survey; the subdimension information exchange between clinical staff reaches 23.3%.
findings.detail: BMG interim report, 1,592 hospitals, self-reported, 2024. Other subdimensions: access to information 71.5%, interoperability 56.4%, data management 36.9%, decision support 29.0%. The values are not broken down by vendor.
findings.source: DigitalRadar Zwischenbericht 2025, BMG
findings.talk_use: National context: access is digital, but decision support and exchange lag.

findings.claim: Only 33.7% of surveyed German gynaecologists would recommend their hospital information system; 52.2% were dissatisfied with reporting and analysis.
findings.detail: DGGG commission survey, 89 respondents, 2022, all vendors; ORBIS most common with 32.6%. No satisfaction results per vendor.
findings.source: Pfob et al., Arch Gynecol Obstet 308:1823
findings.talk_use: Evidence that analysis functions are a weak spot; do not present it as an ORBIS score.

findings.claim: Infection control staff in German hospitals had to extract data from different fields or documents, and relevant information was sometimes buried in free text or physician letters.
findings.detail: Qualitative multi-centre interview study across care levels; systems mentioned include i.s.h.med, ORBIS, medico and Soarian. The problem is not specific to one vendor.
findings.quote: sometimes buried between different diagnoses in free-text fields or unstructured physician’s letters
findings.source: Eisenmann et al., Antimicrob Resist Infect Control 2024
findings.talk_use: Shows the same pattern outside research and across vendors.

findings.claim: The French data protection authority fined Dedalus Biologie 1.5 million EUR in 2022 after data of almost 500,000 people leaked.
findings.detail: Concerns French laboratory software and data migration, so a sister company and not ORBIS. Failings: no encryption, no authentication on the public server area. The CNIL page naming the company is no longer available.
findings.source: GDPR Enforcement Tracker ETid-1136 (also Orrick, April 2022)
findings.talk_use: Only for Q&A on security; always add that it was not ORBIS.

caveats: Most ORBIS feature statements come from the vendor; no independent evaluation of any ORBIS LLM function was found.
UKM MeDIC pages are undated and may be out of date; verify with MeDIC.

KLAS gives mixed signals: Best in KLAS three times, 100% would buy again (Dedalus summary) and 8.0 of 9.0 average satisfaction (HIT Consultant), while KLAS itself describes unmet expectations across the DACH market.
Installation counts differ: over 1,300 in DACH (Blitz 2021), more than 800 hospitals (Dedalus), 821 in Germany and 930 in DACH (reseller page, 2024).
DigitalRadar means appear as 42.1 (Aerzteblatt print, preliminary), 42.5 (Aerzteblatt online) and 42.4 (BMG report); use 42.4. It is self-reported.
The DKI figure of 3 hours of documentation per physician per day (400 hospitals, Sept 2025) is a blanket estimate by the hospitals.
The Charite exclusion of Dedalus was formal and says nothing about product quality.
DigitalRadar, gynaecology and infection control results are not vendor specific.
The MEDA-PKD time comparison is exploratory (n=7, unblinded, by the developers).
gaps: ORBIS-specific SUS or user satisfaction scores: none found.
Native full-text or semantic search in classic ORBIS and HYDMedia: no public documentation found; do not claim that it does not exist.
Public list of UKM systems besides ORBIS (PDMS, RIS/PACS, LIS): not found.
Current gematik ISiK confirmation of ORBIS beyond stage 1 was not checked in the register.
Ardian sale or price increases 2025/2026: no reliable source found; last confirmed fact is the 92% stake agreed in October 2023.
CCC or CVE findings on ORBIS: none found.
ORBIS reporting or SQL access documentation was not found.
The web search budget ran out; UKM LLM pilots on ORBIS letters, MeDIC FHIR pipelines and Trials4Care results were not searched.
